about.label: 02 / The Founder & Mission
about.title: Igor Savitsky: The Louvre in the Sands
about.savitskyQuote: “I wanted to rescue art that was doomed to disappear.”
about.paragraph1: In the remote desert capital of Nukus, artist and archaeologist Igor Savitsky established one of the world’s most extraordinary cultural sanctuaries. Defying ideological suppression, he gathered over 40,000 banned Russian and Soviet avant-garde masterpieces.
about.paragraph2: Alongside this treasure, Savitsky documented the endangered heritage of the Karakalpak people—collecting exquisite textiles, jewelry, and ritual artifacts that would otherwise have been lost to time.

collection.intro: The second-largest collection of Russian avant-garde art in the world, alongside ancient Khorezmian artifacts and Karakalpak ethnographic treasures.

visitPage.intro: Nukus, Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan. Open Tuesday through Sunday.

transit.detail: Nukus Airport (NCU) serves domestic flights from Tashkent. Taxis available outside arrivals.
Nukus Railway Station connects to Tashkent and other Uzbek cities. Journey from Tashkent approx. 18–20 hours.
Taxis and shared minibuses operate throughout Nukus. The museum is centrally located.

faqs.question: Can I take photographs in the museum?
faqs.answer: Personal, non-commercial photography without flash is permitted in permanent exhibition galleries. Tripods and professional equipment require prior written permission.

faqs.question: Is the museum accessible for visitors with disabilities?
faqs.answer: The main museum building is wheelchair accessible with ramp access, lifts between floors and accessible restrooms. Audio guides are available in English and Russian.

faqs.question: Is there a cloakroom or luggage storage?
faqs.answer: A cloakroom is available near the main entrance and is free to use. Large bags, backpacks and luggage must be deposited before entering the galleries.

faqs.question: Does the museum have a café or restaurant?
faqs.answer: A small café is located in the museum courtyard serving tea, coffee and light refreshments during open hours.

faqs.question: Is there a museum shop?
faqs.answer: The museum shop is located near the main entrance and carries exhibition catalogues, art books, postcards, reproductions and Karakalpak craft items.

faqs.question: How long does a typical visit take?
faqs.answer: A standard visit to the permanent collection takes approximately 1.5 to 2 hours. Visitors wishing to explore in depth should allow 2.5 to 3 hours.

faqs.question: Can I visit without booking in advance?
faqs.answer: Walk-in visitors are welcome. Tickets can be purchased at the entrance. Guided tours and group visits should be booked in advance.

faqs.question: Does the museum offer research or archive access?
faqs.answer: The museum archive and study room are accessible to accredited researchers by appointment. Contact research@museum.kr.uz with your research purpose.
